traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: This report covers three sample-size/type categories (❶ 30 g, ❷ 375 g, ❸ environmental samples), each subdivided into three sub-categories (a, b, c). I selected the primary/canonical category ❶ (Infant formula and infant cereals with and without probiotics including ingredients, 30 g sample size) as the main study per the certificate scope's initial validation basis, recording its three sub-categories (a, b, c) from Table 5/6 (page 8-9). The other two category groups found in the same table are: ❷ Infant formula and infant cereals with and without probiotics and ingredients (375 g sample size) - sub-categories a) without probiotics: SEalt 100.0%, SEref 84.6%, RT 90.9%, FPR 0.0%; b) with probiotics: SEalt 100.0%, SEref 81.8%, RT 90.9%, FPR 0.0%; c) ingredients: SEalt 100.0%, SEref 50.0%, RT 77.3%, FPR 0.0%. And ❸ Environmental samples - a) Dusts and residues: SEalt 80.0%, SEref 90.0%, RT 85.0%, FPR 0.0%; b) Cleaning and process water: SEalt 100.0%, SEref 90.0%, RT 95.0%, FPR 0.0%; c) Surface samples (swab, sponge): SEalt 70.0%, SEref 100.0%, RT 85.0%, FPR 0.0%. 'All categories' aggregate row (SEalt 93.1%, SEref 89.1%, RT 90.3%, FPR 0.0%, FNR 0.0%) was excluded as a summary/total row per instructions. FNR was also reported (0.0% for all sub-categories) but is not part of the requested schema fields.
